pharm: Oral small-molecule inhibitor of multiple receptor tyrosine kinases (VEGFR1-3, PDGFR alpha/beta, KIT, FLT3, CSF-1R, RET) that drives antiangiogenic and antitumor activity; the primary metabolite is similarly active.
quick: GIST/RCC: 50 mg once daily, 4 weeks on / 2 weeks off; pNET: 37.5 mg once daily
May be taken with or without food
Can cause fetal harm; effective contraception required
Do not breastfeed during and for 4 weeks after the last dose
No starting-dose change for mild-moderate; limited data on dialysis
Boxed warning - hepatotoxicity can be fatal; monitor LFTs, interrupt/reduce/stop
LFTs each cycle, blood pressure, CBC, thyroid, LVEF/ECG
summary: Sunitinib is an oral multitargeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor used in imatinib-refractory or intolerant GIST, advanced and adjuvant renal cell carcinoma, and progressive well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. It carries a boxed warning for severe and sometimes fatal hepatotoxicity, and requires monitoring of liver function, blood pressure, blood counts, thyroid function and cardiac function.
indications: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) after disease progression on or intolerance to imatinib mesylate
Adjuvant treatment of adults at high risk of recurrent RCC following nephrectomy
Progressive, well-differentiated, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (pNET)

dosage.d: 50 mg orally once daily (Schedule 4/2: 4 weeks on, 2 weeks off)
dosage.t: Until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.n: Adjust in 12.5 mg steps based on tolerability

dosage.d: Consider reducing GIST/RCC dose to 37.5 mg/day (pNET to 25 mg/day)
Consider increasing GIST/RCC dose up to 87.5 mg/day (pNET up to 62.5 mg/day)

admin: Take orally once daily, with or without food
Maintain the assigned 4-weeks-on / 2-weeks-off schedule for GIST/RCC; pNET is continuous
Obtain baseline liver function tests, blood pressure, CBC and thyroid function
Interrupt, dose reduce, or discontinue for hepatotoxicity, heart failure, severe hypertension, or other significant toxicity per the prescribing information
Adjust dose in 12.5 mg increments based on individual safety and tolerability
moa: Sunitinib is a small molecule that inhibits multiple receptor tyrosine kinases implicated in tumor growth, pathologic angiogenesis and metastatic progression, including PDGFR alpha and beta, VEGFR1, VEGFR2 and VEGFR3, KIT, FLT3, CSF-1R and RET. By inhibiting phosphorylation of these receptors it blocks downstream signaling, producing antiangiogenic and direct antitumor effects. Its primary metabolite has similar potency.

relative: Severe pre-existing hepatic impairment or active liver disease
Recent cardiovascular event or significant heart failure
QT prolongation or congenital long QT syndrome
monitor: Thyroid function and complete blood count

preg: Can cause fetal harm based on mechanism and animal findings (embryolethality and teratogenicity). Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for 4 weeks after the last dose; avoid in pregnancy unless benefit outweighs risk.
lact: Sunitinib and its metabolite are excreted in milk in animals. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 4 weeks after the last dose due to the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed child.
renal: No starting-dose adjustment is recommended for mild to severe renal impairment; pharmacokinetics are not markedly affected because elimination is largely hepatic/fecal. Data in patients on dialysis are limited; monitor and adjust based on tolerability.
hepatic: BOXED WARNING: hepatotoxicity can be severe and, in some cases, fatal, including liver failure. Monitor liver function at baseline, during each cycle, and as clinically indicated. Interrupt for Grade 3 hepatotoxicity until recovery to <=Grade 1 or baseline and resume at a reduced dose; discontinue permanently for Grade 4 hepatotoxicity, recurrence, or signs of liver failure.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors - ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir, grapefruit (increase sunitinib levels; reduce dose or avoid)
Strong CYP3A4 inducers - rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, St. John's wort (decrease sunitinib levels; increase dose or avoid)
QT-prolonging drugs and antiarrhythmics (additive torsade risk)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice (CYP3A4 inhibition).
interactions.alcohol: Avoid due to additive hepatic burden.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor ECG/QTc and electrolytes in patients at higher risk; monitor TSH for thyroid dysfunction.

serious: Heart failure / decreased LVEF, myocardial ischemia/infarction
QT prolongation and torsade de pointes
emergency: Acute heart failure or myocardial infarction

monitoring: Liver function tests at baseline, each cycle, and as indicated
LVEF and ECG/QTc in at-risk patients
counsel: Take once daily with or without food, and follow the on/off treatment schedule exactly
Skin and hair may turn yellow; this is expected and reversible
Report yellowing of eyes/skin, dark urine, severe fatigue, or right upper abdominal pain (liver injury)
Report chest pain, breathlessness, leg swelling, or palpitations
Monitor and report high blood pressure and any significant bleeding
Avoid grapefruit; tell your team about all other medicines
Use effective contraception; do not breastfeed during and for 4 weeks after the last dose
pk: Steady state reached in 10-14 days with daily dosing
Tmax 6-12 hours after an oral dose
Store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C); dispense in tight containers
pearls: Boxed warning: hepatotoxicity can be fatal - monitor LFTs at baseline and each cycle
GIST/RCC use the 4-weeks-on/2-weeks-off (Schedule 4/2) regimen; pNET is dosed continuously at 37.5 mg
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers require dose adjustment; avoid grapefruit
Watch for hypertension, hypothyroidism, decreased LVEF and hand-foot syndrome
Hold before major surgery due to impaired wound healing
missed: If a dose is missed, do not take an extra dose; take the next dose at the usual time the following day. Contact the oncology team if more than one dose is missed.
overdose: No specific antidote. Provide general supportive care; if recent, consider emesis or gastric lavage to remove unabsorbed drug. Manage adverse effects consistent with the known safety profile.
